proof:
# A strictly exposed source-fiber point pays a through-source profile

Let d>=1, let C be a compact convex body, and let S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d) have finitely many nonempty full-dimensional fibers. Write eta for the sum of H_{d-1} on their boundaries, with counting measure when d=1. Let Y=(p,y) belong to S with y in the interior of K_p. Fix a finite list of closed halfspaces through Y,

    H_j={a_j dot(z-p)+u_j dot(x-y)>=0}, u_j!=0,

and weights theta_j>=0 summing to one. Let W=sum theta_j 1_{H_j}. No criticality or balance is required for this lemma.

**Lemma.** If there is a ray v from y avoiding all u_j-perpendicular directions, whose endpoint X=(p,x) on boundary K_p is an exposed point of C and has W(X)>=1/2, then a nonnegative convex affine-hinge potential Phi(z,x) has positive finite eta integral and

    integral Phi W d eta / integral Phi d eta = W(X)>=1/2.

Proof. Each cap sign at X is strict, since x-y is a positive multiple of v. Thus there is a neighborhood U of X on which every cap indicator, and hence W, is constant. Shrink U so it contains no other integer base fiber. Choose an exposing affine functional ell with maximum c on C attained uniquely at X. Compactness gives sup_{C outside U} ell<c. Choose delta>0 smaller than this gap and set

    Phi(w)=[ell(w)-c+delta]_+.

This is nonnegative and convex on the full ambient space and vanishes on C outside U. Its value at X is delta. Its integral over boundary K_p is positive: for d>=2, every sufficiently small relatively open boundary neighborhood of a full-dimensional convex body has positive H_{d-1} measure; one can see this by radially projecting a small open set of directions from y onto the boundary, or by a local graph chart. For d=1, X is one of the two counted endpoints. Finiteness follows from boundedness and the finite surface measure of finitely many convex bodies. The support of Phi on eta is contained in U, where W is constant, proving the identity.

**Corollary.** If C is strictly convex, every such through-source profile admits a potential of efficiency at least 1/2.

Choose a vector v avoiding the finitely many hyperplanes u_j dot v=0. The two opposite ray endpoints X_+,X_- in boundary K_p have complementary strict cap signs, so W(X_+)+W(X_-)=1. Select the one with value at least 1/2. Every boundary point of a strictly convex compact body is exposed: a supporting hyperplane exists there, and two points of contact would put their segment on the boundary, contradicting strict convexity. The selected fiber endpoint is on boundary C, since an interior point of C would be interior in its fiber. Apply the lemma.

This does not establish efficiency for arbitrary C. Exposing an entire facet is insufficient to localize its interior with a convex hinge. In the exact product-profile counterexample the cone optimum is below Gamma_d; strictly convex perturbations may admit highly concentrated hinges, with no upper semicontinuity of the optimized potential efficiency at the limiting body. No general-body limiting argument or variational existence theorem follows from this corollary.
